name: Bryan Sutton
notes: The flatpicked-guitar idiom's benchmark. The section's own scope note says why this entry looks the way it does: "in this archetype the producer role is largely occupied by instrumental specialists — the players whose parts are the train beat when there is no drum kit, and who also produce records. Each entry below is written as a parameter set for the part they contribute, because that is what the engine needs." His entry states the guitar's two jobs and one of them is literally a drum kit: "boom-chuck rhythm (bass note on 1 and 3, damped strum on 2 and 4 = literally the two-beat kick and the backbeat in one instrument)". So `kick.densityPerBar` is a flat 2 on anchors 1 and 3, `bassline.register` is raised to 33–44 because "on drummerless tracks with no upright the guitar is simultaneously bass, kick and snare" and the guitar's low strings sit an octave above an upright (the ceiling stops one semitone under the inherited chord floor of 45, since `coherence.rs` needs the generated bass to stay below the generated chords), and the hat lane carries the continuous flatpicked 16ths at reduced velocity. The lead job is described in a sourced phrase — "a unique blend of staccato mixed with powerful chromatic and melodic movements" — glossed in the entry as "high staccato gate (short notes), continuous 8ths/16ths, and chromatic approach notes into chord tones — which is a different melodic rule from the pentatonic/diatonic bluegrass norm". That is `articulation` staccato, `densityPerBar` [8,14], `halfStepDissonance` 0.2 (the highest in this section) and `chordToneBias` dropped to 0.66 so the approach notes land off the chord. Keys are the stated guitar-native G, C, D, A, E with capo transposition, and harmony is "I–IV–V frames with modal ♭VII, and the fiddle-tune repertoire's characteristic I–IV–I–V eight-bar halves", which is why those two families share top weight. Crosspicked passages are the stated textural contrast, so the countermelody is arp-led at `densityRatio` 0.7. ⚠ INFERRED: `bpm.mode` 155 inside the stated 100–210, the velocity tiers, the −5 ms anticipated offset, `percs` contents and the countermelody numbers. ⚠ The entry rates itself medium-high with "awards, era and the technique description sourced verbatim" — the technique quote above is that verbatim source, and the numbers attached to it are this author's reading of it. ⚠ **`drums.hihat.base` widened to the two note values the entry names (2026-08-17, drum variety floor).** `drum_variety::report_how_many_distinct_beats_each_artist_writes` measured 19 distinct beats in 200 seeds against a floor of 20, and its hat column showed **9** — the narrowest hat lane on the roster. The cause is mechanical: at a flat `base: "16th"` with `continuous: true` every sixteenth of every bar is already an onset, so the `fillDensity` of 0.052 authored beside it has no gap left to fill and can move nothing, and the lane writes one identical stream at every seed. The entry's own phrase for this right hand is both note values — the sourced technique line is glossed as "high staccato gate (short notes), **continuous 8ths/16ths**, and chromatic approach notes into chord tones" — and this is the lane the entry's "the hat lane carries the continuous flatpicked 16ths at reduced velocity" assigns that right hand to. On an 8th draw the stream has gaps again and `fillDensity` is live. ⚠ INFERRED: the 3:2 split, and the reading that applies the entry's "continuous 8ths/16ths" — a phrase the entry attaches to the lead job — to the hat lane that carries the same flatpicking. The 16th keeps the top weight because "continuous flatpicked 16ths" is what the note says the lane is. Nothing else moved: `kick` is still the flat 2 on anchors 1 and 3 that "bass note on 1 and 3" states, and the velocities are untouched.
